title: 2025 AMC 12A Problem 11
statement: The orthocenter of a triangle is the concurrent intersection of the three (possibly extended) altitudes. What is the sum of the coordinates of the orthocenter of the triangle whose vertices are \(A(2, 31),\) \(B(8, 27),\) and \(C(18, 27)?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(B\) and \(C\) both have \(y = 27,\) side \(BC\) is horizontal and the altitude from \(A\) is the vertical line \(x = 2.\)

Side \(AC\) has slope \(\dfrac{27 - 31}{18 - 2} = -\dfrac{1}{4},\) so the altitude from \(B\) has slope \(4\): \[y - 27 = 4(x - 8).\]

At \(x = 2,\) \(y = 27 + 4(2 - 8) = 3.\) The orthocenter is \((2, 3),\) with coordinate sum \(5.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: \(B\) and \(C\) share \(y = 27,\) so the altitude from \(A\) is the vertical line \(x = 2\)
The altitude from \(B\) is perpendicular to \(AC\); intersect it with \(x = 2\)
